claims.text: Replacing 20% of the Hf in as-cast HfMoTaTiZr with Sc will reduce alloy density.
Replacing 20% of the Hf with Sc will preserve the strong room-temperature mechanical performance of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Replacing 20% of the Hf with Sc will preserve the strong high-temperature mechanical performance of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Sc substitution will cause grain refinement.
Sc substitution will provide solid-solution strengthening.
Sc has a lower atomic mass than Hf.
The lower atomic mass of Sc relative to Hf will reduce alloy density when Sc replaces Hf.
The modified alloy will retain a solid-solution-strengthening effect sufficient to maintain yield strength.
The modified alloy will have a density no greater than 9.7 g cm−3, representing a reduction of at least 5% from the baseline.
The modified alloy will have a room-temperature yield strength of at least 1500 MPa.
The modified alloy will have a yield strength of at least 800 MPa at 1000 °C.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has an elevated-temperature yield strength of 855 MPa.
Performance is claimed over a temperature range from room temperature to 1600 °C under loading up to yield.
The controlled experiment will compare Sc substitution ratios of 0%, 10%, 20%, and 30%.
Density and yield strength at room temperature and 1000 °C will be measured.
The hypothesis will be rejected if density decreases by less than 3% or if yield strength at room temperature or 1000 °C decreases by more than 10% relative to the baseline.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires at least a 5% density reduction, but the rejection rule permits a 3–5% reduction without falsifying the hypothesis. Likewise, the predicted strength floors correspond to losses of roughly 6–6.5%, whereas the rejection rule permits losses up to 10%.
The claimed boundary extends to 1600 °C, but the experiment measures high-temperature strength only at 1000 °C and therefore cannot test preservation of performance through 1600 °C.

The baseline assigns 855 MPa only to an unspecified 'elevated temperature,' while the prediction and comparison use 1000 °C; the baseline temperature needed for that quantitative comparison is not explicitly established.
